feedback: The confession follows the available contradiction closely: Tess admits the glass was already bare and that her wrapping story concealed an unattended opportunity. Taking poison during the preview specifies the moment but does not supply a missing decisive link, because that source and access were already established. Her wish to acquire authority, rather than mechanically inherit a seat, makes the family grievance more coherent. The last image of the silent family house is emotionally effective without overexplaining the evidence. Chip and Barb's admissions also maintain consequences for nonmurderous wrongdoing. I would have liked slightly more prior emphasis on Tess's desire for authority, but the reveal feels earned and confirms a pre-vote inference.
